about.title: Portola Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Portola is a small mountain town, but its roads still see collisions worth taking seriously. Recent public records show injury crashes clustered on corridors like Rt 70, Grizzly Road, and the 5th/6th Avenue area, with Saturday mornings between 9 and 11 a.m. showing up more often than other times. Whether you were driving, riding along, or walking near one of these corridors, the days right after a crash matter. Insurance adjusters may call quickly, sometimes before you've seen a doctor or understood the full extent of your injuries. LawProactive doesn't practice law or negotiate your claim — we simply connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who can review your situation, explain your options under California law, and help you avoid mistakes that could weaken a future claim. There's no cost to get connected, and no obligation to move forward.

items.title: California's Filing Clock Is Limited
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a car accident claim in California, though claims against a government entity — like a road defect on a county-maintained stretch — can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you're partly at fault for the crash, just reduced by your share of responsibility. That makes it important not to accept blame or give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney.

items.title: No Cap on What You Can Seek for Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, or emotional distress in a car accident case. Contingency-fee representation means you can get an attorney's help evaluating that value without paying anything upfront.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim after a crash in Portola?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government road or agency in Plumas County was involved — for example, a hazard on a county-maintained road — the notice deadline can be as short as six months. Speaking with an attorney early helps make sure you don't miss a shorter window.

items.question: Should I give a statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other insurer before talking to an independent attorney. Insurers often use early statements, made before you know the full extent of your injuries, to minimize what they later offer. An attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: Are crashes near Rt 70 or Grizzly Road in Portola common?
items.answer: Public crash records show injury collisions occurring on corridors like Rt 70, Grizzly Road, and near 5th and 6th Avenues, with Saturday mornings between 9 and 11 a.m. appearing more frequently than other times. These are neutral collision counts, not a judgment about any particular road. If you were involved in a crash on one of these routes, an attorney can help you understand your options.
